1.explanation:
• src/js/components/Select/Select.js — This is where the Select component renders the down-arrow icon (usually via a FormDown or ArrowDown component) and applies its color. The logic here must pick a contrasting color when the background is dark.
• src/js/components/Select/SelectContainer.js — This wrapper propagates background and styling props into the Select display. It influences how the icon color is resolved against the container’s background.
• src/js/components/Select/index.js — The entry point defines defaultProps (including default icons) and theme keys for Select. Adjustments here (for example adding a default icon color or theme mapping) ensure all variants pick up the correct color.
• src/js/themes/dark.js — The dark theme currently lacks a specific override for Select icon color, so it falls back to the border/text color, which on dark backgrounds makes the arrow invisible. Adding a theme.select.icons.down.color (or adjusting global.control/text color) here will provide a visible contrast on dark-1 backgrounds.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a Select inside a dark-1 background container, the default dropdown arrow icon blends into the surrounding border and background and becomes effectively invisible. In the example, a <Select> with placeholder “Select” on a dark-1 box shows no visible arrow. On a light background the arrow renders in purple (as expected), but on a dark background it draws in the same color as the border/placeholder and is lost.

2.explanation:
• src/js/components/Select/Select.js: This file instantiates the down-arrow icon and applies its default color. It needs to pull in a contrasting (light) color when placed on a dark background.
• src/js/components/Select/SelectContainer.js: This wrapper wires up the Select control styling and passes theme colors to the icon. Adjustments here will ensure the right color prop reaches the icon based on background.
• src/js/themes/dark.js: The dark theme currently doesn’t define a contrasting color for control icons on dark-1. Extending the dark theme (for example adding global.control.icons.down.color or overriding global.colors.text-strong) will allow the arrow to render in a light shade on dark backgrounds.
2.bug_scenario: When using a <Select> inside a dark background (dark-1) container the built-in down‐arrow icon is effectively invisible. The component renders the arrow in the theme’s default “text” (dark) color, so on a dark-1 background it disappears. In the Codesandbox reproduction, the Select placeholder shows but no arrow appears in the dark box, whereas on a white background the arrow shows normally.
